chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Yunus bin Ya'qoub, from Shu'aib al-Aqraqoufi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

There is something narrated from Abu Dharr, upon whom is the mercy of Allah, that he used to say: 'Three things which the people hate, and which I love: I love death, and I love poverty, and I love tribulation.' He said: Indeed, this is not as they narrate. He only meant: Death in obedience to Allah is more beloved to me than life in disobedience to Allah, and poverty in obedience to Allah is more beloved to me than wealth in disobedience to Allah, and tribulation in obedience to Allah is more beloved to me than health in disobedience to Allah.
ai.seo_question: Why did Abu Dharr say he loved death and poverty if people generally hate them?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this clarification to resolve the apparent paradox in Abu Dharr’s asceticism, emphasizing that the value of death, poverty, and tribulation is contingent upon their role in facilitating obedience to Allah. This interpretation aligns with the Shia scholarly understanding that worldly states are neutral, deriving their spiritual merit from whether they lead to or away from divine pleasure. The Imam’s explanation underscores the principle that enduring hardship for God’s sake is superior to enjoying comfort in sin.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed, from Ibn Faddal, from Yunus bin Ya’qoub, from Shu’aib al-‘Aqraqoufi, that he said: I said to Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him:

There is something narrated from Abu Dharr, upon whom is the mercy of Allah, that he used to say: «Three things which the people hate, and which I love: I love death, and I love povery, and I love tribulation.» Then he said: Indeed, this is not like as they narrate. He only meant: Death in obedience to Allah is more beloved to me than life in disobedience to Allah, and poverty in obedience to Allah is more beloved to me than wealth in disobedience to Allah, and tribulation in obedience to Allah is more beloved to me than health in disobedience to Allah.
